extracted.intended_audience: British scientific community, agriculturalists, and policymakers (Victorian-era readership of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for instituting and carrying out a formal investigation (commission) into the potato blight: what questions to ask, what data to collect, and what institutional arrangements and experimental standards are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of commission inquiry (Origin, Cause, Remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission would have to inquire into the Origin, Cause, and Remedies for the Potato Disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the investigation explicitly around origin, causal factors, and practicable remedies; set up a formal body (preferably government-led) to carry out sustained, systematic inquiry rather than ad hoc private efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate prevalence by soil type
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the disease is most prevalent on any particular soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and compare incidence data across different soil types to test associations between soil characteristics and disease prevalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare overwintered seed vs spring-sown seed immunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, as some assert, seed left in the ground through the winter enjoys comparative immunity as contrasted with that sown in the spring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design comparative field studies tracking seed provenance and sowing date; control for confounders and document outcomes across seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess safety of imported/introduced seed versus local seed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether seed introduced from a distance is safer than that grown in the neighbourhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include provenance in seed selection experiments; compare disease incidence for locally-produced seed versus imported seed under the same cultivation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varietal susceptibility (old varieties versus new)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether old varieties are dying out and new ones comparatively healthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out varietal trials, record varietal histories and health outcomes, and determine whether certain cultivars exhibit resistance or susceptibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical timing threshold for crop safety (August 10 test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, if the disease can by any means be warded off till August 10, the crop is then comparatively safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the stage-dependence of susceptibility and whether survival past a specific calendar/date threshold markedly reduces risk; use longitudinal observations across seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation with thundery weather and electrical disturbance
rubrics_metrics.description: On one point almost all authorities are agreed, viz., that the disease generally makes its first decided appearance during thundery weather. The exceptional amount of electrical disturbance ... appears to have been most unfavourable to the potato crop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect meteorological data concurrent with disease outbreaks (thunderstorms, electrical activity) to test correlation/causation hypotheses; compare regions with differing thunderstorm frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with other epidemics and periodicity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is worthy of note that an unusual development of the potato blight has been hitherto accompanied by murrain or epidemic diseases in animals and in other crops, and that a certain periodicity appears to be manifested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile historical records of plant and animal epidemics to assess co-occurrence patterns and possible cyclical behavior (e.g., ~12-year intervals); use statistical analysis of temporal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic collection and tabulation of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be difficult to collect the facts; but they have never yet been tabulated or presented to the public in such a form that any conclusions can be drawn unquestionably from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute standardized data collection protocols and tabulate observations so that robust, reproducible conclusions can be drawn; publish datasets and methods transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate starch viability and economic salvage
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Hooker has given ... the starch of the potato is not affected by the complaint, if only some economical mode can be found of separating it from the diseased ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include analyses of which crop components remain usable (e.g., starch) and develop economical processing or salvage methods as part of remedies research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer government-led, institutional investigations over ad hoc private efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: We are, therefore, driven once more to the third alternative; and compelled to inquire whether we have not a right to look to the Government of the country to 'interfere' in the matter ... to institute and to promote an investigation into the Origin, Cause, and Remedies for the Potato Disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nationally-significant agricultural epidemics, organize sustained, publicly funded investigations (commissions/official institutions) rather than relying solely on private benefactors or local societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use validated, modern analytical methods (avoid outdated tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: The method employed for the estimation of the sulphur is not stated; it is to be hoped ... that one of the more recent methods has been adopted, and not the 'Letheby sulphur test,' which, as is well known, gives at the best, most inaccurate results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify and use up-to-date, validated analytical methods in reporting chemical/quantitative results; explicitly state methods used and avoid known-inaccurate tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental apparatus should automatically record measurements and report uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments were performed with carefully made apparatus, which automatically recorded the resistance and the speed, and the errors and uncertainties of the results probably did not in any case exceed on the whole 4 per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instrumentation that automatically logs key variables (reducing observer bias), estimate and report measurement uncertainties (aiming for low percentage errors), and disclose error bounds with results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control confounding factors (e.g., eliminate thickness resistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Great pains were taken, and successfully, to eliminate, and, indeed in effect to obliterate the resistance due to thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and control or eliminate confounding physical factors in experiments (document control measures) to isolate the effect under study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate multiple relations and acknowledge interdependence of variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects of the three conditions ... could not be regarded as absolutely independent of each other, because certain variations in the quality of the surfaces were found to affect in some degree the relations of the force to the speed and to the length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments and analyses to detect interactions among variables; do not assume independence without testing; discuss interdependencies in interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare coatings/surface qualities and lengths systematically
rubrics_metrics.description: These are, (1) the relation of the force to the speed, (2) its relation to the quality of the surface, (3) its relation to the length of the surface along the line of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying friction/resistance, systematically vary speed, surface quality/coating, and length, and report the functional relations observed (including power-law fits where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicate trials to observe changes over time (e.g., slime growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the surface coated with glue, and thus simulating the sliminess of a living fish, three successive experiments were tried at the same speed, so as to test the effect of the gradual growth of the slimy character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform repeated trials to observe temporal evolution of surface/experimental conditions; use replication to quantify progressive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present tabular summaries with stated applicability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The following tabular statement gives the mean resistance per square foot on surfaces of from 1 foot to 50 feet in length, with speeds of from 200 to 800 feet per minute. The table is applicable to a clean planed surface coated either with shellac varnish, Hay's or Peacock's composition, or tallow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear tabular data summarizing mean results, and explicitly state the conditions under which the table applies (surface treatments, speed ranges, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and report reliability of second-hand/topographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not surprising that such discrepancies should exist, when it is known that the best maps have been compiled with no better materials than the reports of natives, and that none but a very small portion of the entire region has ever been traversed by civilised men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For geographical/topographical claims, prioritize direct observation and instrumented measurement; treat unverified native reports and second-hand information with caution and explicitly assess their reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirically verify cartographic claims and correct map errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The map ... which is decidedly the best that has hitherto appeared, is defective in representing the main chain as arising abruptly from the low country ... The remarkable valley ... must be pronounced imaginary or based on false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify significant map features by direct reconnaissance where possible; correct or flag clearly erroneous features (e.g., imaginary valleys) rather than accepting prior maps uncritically.
